title: Easy Sheet Pan Sausage and Veggies (30-Minute Family Dinner)
contentHtml:
Easy sheet pan sausage and veggies is a simple 30-minute family dinner with smoky sausage, crisp-tender vegetables, and almost no cleanup.

This is the kind of dinner that works when you want something hearty without babysitting three pans. Everything roasts together, cleanup is easy, and the recipe is flexible enough to use what you already have in the fridge.

Photo: Gwen via Wikimedia Commons, source, licensed under CC BY 2.0. No changes made.

Why This Sheet Pan Dinner Works

  • Fast: dinner is on the table in about 30 minutes.
  • Easy cleanup: one pan handles the whole meal.
  • Family-friendly: sausage, potatoes, and roasted vegetables are simple and familiar.
  • Flexible: swap vegetables based on what you have.

Easy Sheet Pan Sausage and Veggies Recipe

Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 20 minutes
Total time: 30 minutes
Servings: 6

Equipment

  • Large rimmed sheet pan
  • Cutting board and knife
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Spatula

Ingredients

  • 14 ounces fully cooked smoked sausage or kielbasa, sliced into 1/2-inch rounds
  • 1 pound baby potatoes, quartered
  • 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 1 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 1 medium zucchini, cut into thick half-moons
  • 1 small red onion, cut into wedges
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
  • 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon chopped parsley, optional

Instructions

  1. Heat the oven. Preheat to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment or foil if you want even easier cleanup.
  2. Give the potatoes a head start. Place the quartered potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons water. Cover and microwave for 4 minutes, then drain well. This keeps the whole recipe on a 30-minute timeline.
  3. Season everything. In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, sausage, bell peppers, zucchini, and onion. Add olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Toss until evenly coated.
  4. Roast. Spread everything in a single layer on the sheet pan. Roast for 10 minutes.
  5. Flip and finish. Stir or flip the sausage and vegetables, then roast another 8 to 10 minutes until the potatoes are tender, the vegetables have browned edges, and the sausage is hot throughout.
  6. Serve. Sprinkle with parsley if using and serve straight from the pan.

Easy Substitutions

  • Sausage: turkey sausage, chicken sausage, kielbasa, or another fully cooked sausage all work.
  • Vegetables: broccoli, green beans, Brussels sprouts, mushrooms, or carrots are good swaps.
  • Potatoes: Yukon Gold or red potatoes work; cut them into small, even pieces.
  • Spice: add crushed red pepper or Cajun seasoning if your family likes heat.

Cooking Tips

  • Do not overcrowd the pan or the vegetables will steam instead of roast.
  • Cut everything to similar sizes so it finishes at the same time.
  • Use a large sheet pan; two smaller pans are better than one overloaded pan.
  • If your sausage package gives a reheating temperature, follow that label guidance.

What to Serve With Sheet Pan Sausage and Veggies

This is a full meal on its own, but garlic bread, a green salad, or a simple mustard dipping sauce all work well on the side.

Storage and Reheating

Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 to 4 days. Reheat in a 375°F oven or air fryer until hot, or microwave individual portions. The oven or air fryer will keep the vegetables crisper.

Estimated Nutrition

Estimated per serving: about 330 calories, 13g protein, 28g carbohydrates, and 19g fat. Actual values vary based on the sausage brand and vegetables used.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make sheet pan sausage and veggies ahead of time?

Yes. Chop the vegetables and sausage up to a day ahead, store them separately or together in the refrigerator, and season just before roasting.

Can I use raw sausage?

You can, but the timing changes and the sausage must reach the safe internal temperature specified for that type of meat. This version is written for fully cooked sausage so the vegetables and sausage finish together.

How do I keep the vegetables from getting soggy?

Use high heat, spread everything in a single layer, avoid overcrowding, and dry washed vegetables well before seasoning.

This is an original The Man That Cooks Sometimes recipe created for an easy weeknight family dinner.
